audit_name: M12 Study 5 independent source and finite-exposure review

author_exact12_efetch.order_and_uniqueness: Selected 12 IDs returned in the fixed pair order; 12 unique.

broad141_efetch.order_and_uniqueness: Requested and returned IDs matched in exact order; 141 unique.

candidate_discovery_record.selection: 12 selected from the 141-ID noncollision fetch pool; other candidates retained as not selected, without a claim of exhaustive factual suitability review. Selection was not informed by performance.

review_scope: Independent review of source identity; title, complete authors, DOI, journal, issue/electronic year and PubMed publication types; primary-research status from abstract methods; abstract-level claim scope; literal excerpt integrity and word limits; draft lengths and identifier/title echo; six pair boundaries; and disjointness against the supplied finite exposure manifest.
limits: Abstract-only evidence review; no full-text, figure, methods-section, or supplementary-information review.
No scientific novelty/quality judgment, representative sampling claim, validator-performance screening, maintained-tool search, or model call.
Primary-research classification is based on original methods/results described in the PubMed abstracts plus PubMed Journal Article types; it is not a separate peer-review of each article.
The source-disjointness result applies only to the finite local exposure manifest and its three hashed roots; it is not universal/global freshness or exhaustive literature novelty.
Historical studies 1–4 were not resumed or replayed; this receipt is limited to source validation for the six exploratory pairs.

cross_pair_control_scope_notes.scope: The colorectal cancer control has broad gastrointestinal/epithelial context adjacent to these gut-related positives; its MBD2/SFRP1 epigenetic mechanism differs from the microbial-metabolite transporter axis and hydrogel/organoid intervention.
The Entebbe virus control and influenza A positive are both virology topics but concern different virus systems and processes: envelope-mediated release versus host antiviral ubiquitination.
